Subject: MAP: HelionTech go-live & canary cadence

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, attached is the initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the post-signature implementation plan: rollout phases, controlled canary windows, migration cutover steps, and the training cadence for platform and ops teams. Attachments: helion_map_v1.xlsx, rollout_diagram_v1.png.

High-level asks and next steps I captured:
- Review the timeline (Phase 0–3) and confirm the two-week canary window is acceptable.
- Confirm the list of Helion pilot users for the canary (we suggested the payments and invoicing teams).
- Confirm compliance evidence needs ahead of the audit on Sep 10 (SOC2 evidence bucket).

Summary (embedded MAP highlights):
Phase 0 — Provisioning & Security (Aug 20–26)
  - Redwood: environment provisioning, KMS integration, baseline ingress rules
  - Helion: provide test service accounts + compliance contact
Phase 1 — Canary Ramp (Aug 27–Sep 9)
  - 2-week canary with 10% traffic shift; daily quality evals; automatic rollback gate on error-rate > 3% or latency P95 > 750ms
Phase 2 — Bulk Migration (Sep 10–Sep 17)
  - 48-hour cutover weekend option; DB read-only window; fallback variant pinned for 24h
Phase 3 — Training & Handover (Sep 18–Sep 30)
  - 4 instructor-led sessions, recorded; runbook handback; Q/A office hours for 2 weeks

Evaluation plan (what we'll measure during canary):
- Functional regressions via the shared eval suite (passing threshold: 98% of golden prompts)
- Latency and cost per 1k tokens baseline
- Model output quality: sampling of 200 responses weekly scored by Helion engineers

Deliverables and owners are in the attached MAP spreadsheet. I’ll send an updated version after we incorporate your team’s availability. If this looks good, I’ll also kick off the DocuSign flow for the SOW addendum which includes the dedicated canary run time.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0184

Attachment stubs: helion_map_v1.xlsx (xlsx), rollout_diagram_v1.png (image)

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: HelionTech go-live & canary cadence

Jasmine —

Thanks for the plan and clear breakdown. A few quick asks from our side after reviewing the MAP: 
1) Can we shift the canary start one week later to Sep 3 so we finish the internal security review first (audit on Sep 10 is a hard date).
2) Training: can we do two earlier half-day workshops for the Platform team the week before the canary so they can shadow during the first three days?
3) During the canary, we need daily summary emails with regression highlights sent to our compliance@heliontech.com alias.

On the rollbacks: the error-rate > 3% gate makes sense, but can we add a manual approval step before a rollback is actioned (so our on-call can review within the 30-minute window)?

Also CCing Mateo Silva (our Solutions Architect) to confirm pilot user list. He’ll attach the list in a follow-up.

Samir
VP Engineering, HelionTech
samir@heliontech.com

Subject: Re: MAP: HelionTech go-live & canary cadence

Samir —

Appreciate the feedback — we can accommodate all three asks. Proposed updates and clarifications below (I’ve made these inline edits in helion_map_v2.xlsx which I attached):

- Canary start moved to Sep 3 (Phase 1: Sep 3–Sep 16).
- Training: two half-day instructor-led sessions on Aug 30 and Aug 31 focused on platform ops + troubleshooting; three shorter shadow sessions during Sep 3–Sep 5 (morning overlap) for handoff.
- Daily compliance summaries: Redwood will publish a daily canary digest to compliance@heliontech.com by 10:00 PT each morning during the canary.
- Rollback gating: we will add a manual approval step to the automated rollback. If automated criteria are met (error-rate > 3% or latency P95 > 750ms), Redwood will notify the Helion on-call and wait up to 30 minutes for approval. If no response, we will place the cluster in a hold state and escalate to product ops; full rollback only after manual confirmation unless safety-critical (error-rate > 7%).

Evaluation plan (revised):
- Daily evals: 200-sample randomization run overnight; pass threshold lowered to 97% for the first three days of canary to account for edge-cases; back to 98% thereafter.
- Cost telemetry: per-interval token cost sampling (Redwood to provide per-route breakdown).

Canary checklist (short):
- Pre-canary: smoke tests, synthetic latency test, auth token verification
- Day 0: route 5% traffic, verify logs and KV cache hits
- Day 3: ramp to 25% if quality gates pass
- Day 7: ramp to 50%
- Day 10+: decide on bulk migration cadence

Attachments: helion_map_v2.xlsx, canary_checklist.pdf

Next steps I will take this afternoon: update the HubSpot record, push the revised MAP to Confluence, and start the DocuSign envelope for the addendum. Marissa — can you confirm trainer assignments and the Redwood resource calendar? Vivek — can you confirm that the canary digest automation is scoped for the required telemetry (errors, latency, QA sampling)? Grace — can you own the training recording deliverables and runbook handback?

Thanks —
Jasmine
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
